result.topic_en: The final page of Euler's paper on maxima and minima, stating a theorem that the differential formula Z dx is integrable exactly when N − dP/dx + d²Q/dx² − d³R/dx³ + … vanishes identically; the facing page begins the next paper, 'De insigni promotione methodi tangentium inversae'.
result.transcription:
134 DE METHOD. MAXIM. ET MINIM.

grue accommodatur. Veluti si inter omnes lineas, a dato, puncto non ad aliud punctum, sed ad lineam quandam datam, siue rectam, siue curuam, ducendas, ea requiratur, super qua corpus ab illo puncto descendens tempore breuissimo ad hanc lineam perueniat, per considerationem illarum partium absolutarum hoc problema facile resoluitur, dum iis ista conditio praescribitur, vt curua quaesita ad datam sit normalis. Antequam autem finiam, examini Analystarum egregium Theorema subiiciam, cuius veritas ex principiis hactenus positis haud difficulter perspicitur, et quod in calculo integrali eximium vsum praestare videtur.

Theorema.

Proposita formula differentiali $Zdx$, in qua $Z$ sit functio quaecunque quantitatum $x$, $y$, $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$, $q=\frac{dp}{dx}$, $r=\frac{dq}{dx}$ etc. eaque differentiata prodeat:
$dZ = Mdx + Ndy + Pdp + Qdq + Rdr +$ etc.
ita vt haec formula differentialis $Zdx$ differentialia non solum prima, sed etiam altiora cuiusque ordinis, complectatur; tum facile diiudicari poterit, vtrum ista formula integrationem admittat, siue sit differentiale completum, nec ne? Consideretur enim ista expressio, sumto $dx$ constante,
$V = N - \frac{dP}{dx} + \frac{ddQ}{dx^2} - \frac{d^3R}{dx^3} +$ etc.
quae si reperiatur nihilo aequalis, formula $Zdx$ erit integrabilis; verum si non fuerit $V=0$, ea non erit integrabilis.

DE

[Facing page 135: beginning of the next paper, 'De insigni promotione methodi tangentium inversae', Auctore L. Eulero.]

items.english: For consider this expression, taking dx constant, V = N − dP/dx + ddQ/dx² − d³R/dx³ + etc.; if it is found equal to zero, the formula Z dx will be integrable; but if V is not 0, it will not be integrable.
